Party that sets up a fund, decides upon the investment strategy, appoints agents, and is responsible for the promotion and the marketing of the fund. This party makes all the strategic decisions related to a fund.

Party responsible for keeping track of the owners of securities. In the investment fund business, this party keeps the investor registry of the fund, and administers investor accounts and related records. It is appointed by the fund management company.

Party appointed by the fund management company. This party updates records of investor accounts to reflect the daily investor purchases, redemptions, switches, transfers, and re-registrations. It ensures the timely settlement of transactions, and may provide tax information to the investor and/or to its intermediaries. It may calculate, collect, and rebate commissions. It prepares and distributes confirmations reflecting transactions, resulting in unit or cash account movements to the investor or the investor's intermediary. It responds to inquiries concerning account status, and processes the income distribution.

Party that provides services to investors relating to financial products. These services may include some, or all of, provision of information and advice on products, placement of investment orders, transmission of payment, custody of assets, and the administration of rights and benefits. In the specific framework of investment funds industry, an intermediary may present information about funds to potential investors, and solicit orders for the fund. This intermediary may facilitate the transmission of the orders and information from/to the investors and/or other intermediaries. The intermediary receives commission from the Fund and/or fees from the investor.
Party that act as an wholesaler of funds.
Party that acts as an aggregator of funds, also called a funds hub.
Underlying client of the intermediary.
Underlying client of underlying client 1.
Party that transmits the instruction, advice, notification or report.
Financial instruments held at a local custodian.
Financial instruments held at an International Central Securities Depository.
Financial instruments held at a National Central Securities Depository.
Used for certain financial instruments, for example, US mutual funds, where settlement is internal only, that is, there is no external movement of securities.
Price expressed as a number of percentage points below par, for example, a discount price of 2.0% equals a price of 98 when par is 100.
Price expressed as a number of percentage points above par, for example, a premium price of 2.0% equals a price of 102 when par is 100.
Price is the calculated bid price of a dual-priced fund (offer-bid prices), that is, the selling price of the units for the investor.
Price is the calculated offer price of a dual-priced investment fund (offer-bid prices), that is, the buying price of the units for an investor.
Price is the net asset value per unit that is used either as a transacting price for a single-priced investment fund class, or as a notional price for the calculation of other prices.

Price is the calculated creation price of a dual-priced investment fund (creation-cancellation prices) and the highest possible buying price of the units before the initial charge. The actual buying or offer price, which includes charges, will be higher.

Price is the calculated cancellation price of a dual-priced investment fund (creation-cancellation price), and the lowest possible valuation of the units on any one-day. The actual selling or bid price is usually higher.
Price is the non-official interim price given to an investor before the executed price.

Price is the calculated net asset value price of a single-priced investment fund. The price is adjusted to take into account the dealing costs due to individual large deals, or due to a significant imbalance in volumes of subscriptions vs redemptions, as an alternative to dilution levy.
Price is the average price between the bid and offer prices.
Price is the price used when reinvesting units after distribution.
Price is the price used when transferring units between products.
Price is the current market price.
Price is the estimated indicative price.
Source of price quotation is a fund, eg, transfer agent, fund itself.
Source of price quotation is a theoretical value based on the market yield.
Source of price quotation is an external vendor.
Balance of securities that are blocked or frozen. A financial instrument may be unavailable due to external circumstances such as a court order, death of beneficiary or account owner, or bankruptcy.
Balance of securities that have been borrowed from another party.
Balance of securities that belong to a third party and that are held for the purpose of collateralisation.
Balance of securities that belong to the safekeeping account indicated within this message, and are deposited with a third party for the purpose of collateralisation.
Balance of securities that have been loaned to a third party.
Balance of securities that are used as collateral for derivatives.
Balance of securities pending delivery that have been matched. This is only applicable in a CSD to participant communication.
Balance of securities pending receipt that have been matched. This is only applicable in a CSD to participant communication.
Balance of securities pending receipt that are unmatched. This is only applicable in a CSD to participant communication.
Balance of securities, before ex-date, that are involved in a corporate action (CA). Securities blocked due to a CA, for example, proxi, in escrow, are to be identified in the BLOK sub-balance.
Balance of securities that are pending delivery.
Balance of securities that are pending receipt.
Balance of securities that are pledged, for example, a financial instrument is unavailable because it has been used or given as a guarantee.
Balance of securities pending delivery that are unmatched. This is only applicable in a CSD to participant communication.
Balance of securities currently being processed by the institution responsible for registering the new beneficial owner (or nominee) of securities after a transaction has settled.
Balance of securities that may only be sold under certain conditions or require legal documents.
Balance of securities that is unclassified, ie, is not identified with one of the existing sub-balance types.
Balance of physical securities that are in transshipment, eg, in the process of being transferred from one depository or agent to another.
Balance of securities that are drawn for redemption.
Financial instrument is unavailable due to missing or incomplete documentation pertaining to the account, or due to a missing or incomplete order.
Financial instrument is unavailable as a result of a transfer order, pending movement in the shareholders' register.
Balance of tax-exempt securities.
Balance of taxable securities.
Balance of securities that are registered (in the name of a nominee or of the beneficial owner).
Balance of securities that is unclassified, ie, is not identified with one of the existing sub-balance types.
Balance of securities that remain registered in the name of the prior beneficial owner of securities.
Balance of securities that could not be registered due to foreign ownership limitation.
